messages.content: I want an API that takes an IP address and returns company data with contact information if available.

url.description: The Date Nager API provides access holiday information for over 100 countries, including the ability to query for long weekends. It leverages ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to tailor the search to your specific region of interest. More information can be found in https://date.nager.at/Api

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here are a few well‑known public APIs that accept an IP address (or a CIDR block) and return enriched data about the owner organization, including contact details when available: | Service | Key Features | Typical Endpoint | Pricing / Limits | Notes | |---------|--------------|------------------|------------------|-------| | **ipinfo.io** | • Organization name, ASN, domain, and contact email.
• Geo‑location, carrier, and privacy flags.
• Free tier: 50k requests/month, paid plans start at $5/mo. | `https://ipinfo.io//json` | Free: 50k/month, Paid: $5/mo (50k), $10/mo (200k), etc. | Requires an API token. The “org” field often contains the company name; the “contact” field (if present) gives an email. | | **ipstack.com** | • Company name, domain, and contact email via the “company” object.
• Geo‑location, currency, and timezone.
• Free tier: 10k requests/month, paid plans start at $10/mo. | `https://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=YOUR_KEY&fields=ip,hostname,company,location` | Free: 10k/month, Paid: $10/mo (10k), $20/mo (25k), etc. | The “company” object includes `name`, `domain`, and `email`. | | **ipapi.co** | • Organization name, domain, and contact email.
• Geo‑location, carrier, and ASN.
• Free tier: 30k requests/day, paid plans start at $9.99/mo. | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | Free: 30k/day, Paid: $9.99/mo (200k), etc. | The “org” field contains the company name; “contact” may contain an email. | | **ipgeolocation.io** | • Company name, domain, and contact email via the “organization” object.
• Geo‑location, carrier, and ASN.
• Free tier: 1k requests/day, paid plans start at $19/mo. | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=` | Free: 1k/day, Paid: $19/mo (10k), etc. | The “organization” object includes `name`, `domain`, and `email`. | | **MaxMind GeoIP2 Precision Services** | • Organization name, domain, and contact email via the “Company” object.
• Geo‑location, ASN, and ISP.
• Free tier: 1k requests/day, paid plans start at $49/mo. | `https://geoip.maxmind.com/geoip/v2.1/precision/country/` | Free: 1k/day, Paid: $49/mo (10k), etc. | Requires a license key. The “company” object contains `name`, `domain`, and `email`. | ### How to Use One of These APIs (Example with ipinfo.io) ```bash # Replace YOUR_TOKEN with your actual token curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \ https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json ``` Typical JSON response: ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "hostname": "dns.google", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "US", "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "readme": "https://ipinfo.io/missingauth" } ``` If the IP belongs to a business, the `org` field will contain the company name. Some providers also expose a `contact` field: ```json { "ip": "203.0.113.42", "org": "AS12345 Example Corp", "company": { "name": "Example Corp", "domain": "example.com", "email": "contact@example.com" } } ``` ### Choosing the Right Service | Criteria | ipinfo.io | ipstack.com | ipapi.co | ipgeolocation.io | MaxMind | |----------|-----------|-------------|----------|------------------|---------| | **Free quota** | 50k/month | 10k/month | 30k/day | 1k/day | 1k/day | | **Contact email** | Yes (optional) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | | **Ease of integration** | Simple JSON, optional fields | Simple JSON, optional fields | Simple JSON, optional fields | Simple JSON, optional fields | Requires SDK or HTTP call | | **Pricing** | $5/mo | $10/mo | $9.99/mo | $19/mo | $49/mo | | **Best for high volume** | ipinfo.io | ipapi.co | ipapi.co | ipapi.co | MaxMind | ### Quick Tips 1. **API Keys** – All services require an API key or token. Sign up on their websites to obtain one. 2. **Rate Limits** – Respect the free tier limits; otherwise, you’ll hit throttling or receive incomplete data. 3. **Data Fields** – Not all IPs belong to companies; residential IPs often return only ISP data. Business IPs are more likely to have a `company` object. 4. **Caching** – IP data rarely changes frequently. Cache responses for at least 24–48 hours to reduce API calls. --- #### Next Steps 1. Pick a provider that matches your budget and quota needs. 2. Sign up and get an API key. 3. Test the endpoint with a known business IP (e.g., `8.8.8.8` for Google) to confirm you receive the `company` or `org` fields. 4. Integrate the call into your application, handling missing fields gracefully. Let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into any particular provider, or if you need help writing code to consume one of these APIs!
